_comentario: First Economics, Part 3 (spring, days 131-195): the English text of each day of Aprendo economía -- the day's story ('historia') and the text of its activity ('actividad', with its 'tipo') -- and the words of weeks 27-39 ('semanas'). Everything else is the one in content/q3.json, page by page: see cargar_ingles in tools/gen_economia.py and notes/02-english.md.

semanas.definicion: The money we use today in Spain and in many other countries in Europe.
The money that is used to buy or pay for something.
A place where things are fixed or made, like bikes or cars.
The money you earn by working.
Swapping things among several people, so that everyone gets something new.
A place where things are sold: the baker's, the greengrocer's, the bookshop...
Taking good care of something or someone who depends on you.
The hours and days we use to do things; we can give it as a present, too.
A box or a jar with a slot, for keeping the money you save.
The steps something goes through before it reaches us, like honey: from the flower to the jar.
To use or eat what we buy: food, water, electricity.
A place where money is kept safe, and where you can also borrow money.
To give something in exchange for money.

dias.historia: Marta shows the class a photo from twenty-five years ago: she and her classmates are burying a time capsule. Back then, people paid with pesetas; the euro arrived soon afterwards.

frases: Today in Spain we pay with euros.
Twenty-five years ago, people paid with pesetas.
People pay with euros in many countries.
The euro is older than the peseta.

dias.historia: Marta explains that prices change over the years: things usually cost more now than they used to. Dad knows this well: when he was young, comics were much cheaper.

actividad.texto: Twenty years ago, a comic cost €2, and today it costs €5. How much has the price gone up?

dias.historia: Marta shows them the euro notes and coins we have today. The biggest note the class has seen is a €50 note.

actividad.pregunta: How much money is there here?

dias.historia: Paco has been at the school for thirty years. He remembers the day of the photo, and also the day when pesetas were changed for euros: what a muddle of coins!

actividad.pregunta: In what order did it happen? The story of money
pasos: People swapped things for other things.
In Spain, people paid with pesetas.

dias.historia: Case solved: the photo says “Photo by P.” Pilar is in the photo, holding the spade, and no parents came that day... Paco took it!

checklist: I know what the euro is.
I know that people used to pay with pesetas.
I know that prices change over the years.
actividad.prompt: Draw what you would put in a time capsule.

dias.historia: Lucía wants to make torrijas on her own, as she promised. First, she writes down her spending: the bread, the milk and the eggs. She already has the sugar and the cinnamon at home.

actividad.pregunta: Lucía buys the bread, the milk and the eggs. How much does she spend?

dias.historia: With Grandma's recipe, Lucía makes the torrijas step by step. Dad does only one thing: he fries them, because the oil is very hot.

actividad.pregunta: How are torrijas made?
pasos: The bread is soaked in milk.
It is rolled in sugar and cinnamon.

dias.historia: Lucía writes down in a notebook the money that comes in and the money that goes out: that way she always knows how much she has left. Dad calls it “keeping accounts”.

actividad.pregunta: Lucía's accounts: how much does she have left after each line?

dias.historia: There was one torrija left on the dish, and it has disappeared. The dish was on the high shelf, but nobody has moved the chair. Only Grandma and Toby were at home...

frases: Spending is money we use to pay for something.
If you write down what you spend, you know how much you have left.
Making torrijas at home costs nothing at all.
If you spend more than you have, you have money left over.

dias.historia: Case solved: a trail of sugar goes from the kitchen to Grandma's armchair. She ate it! “It was so delicious that I could not wait,” she says, laughing.

checklist: I know what spending is.
I can write down what comes in and what goes out.
I know how much a recipe costs.
actividad.prompt: Draw your favourite recipe, and what you need to buy to make it.

dias.historia: Lucía's bike has a flat tyre. Dad says there is no need to buy a new one: the workshop on the corner mends punctures, and it costs much less.

actividad.texto: A new tyre costs €25, and mending the puncture costs €8. How much does Lucía save by mending it?

dias.historia: The man at the workshop finds a thorn stuck in the tyre. Then he shows Lucía how to mend a puncture, step by step, so that next time she can do it herself.

actividad.pregunta: How do you mend a puncture?

dias.historia: In the neighbourhood there is a bike workshop, a car garage and a motorbike workshop. But not everything that breaks goes to a workshop: each thing has its own place.

actividad.pregunta: Is it fixed at a workshop?
cosas: a bike with a broken chain
a car that will not start
a tooth with a hole in it
a motorbike with a broken light

dias.historia: Where did the tyre get its puncture? When they left the baker's, it was still hard. Because of the roadworks, Dad carried the bikes... and then they went past the rose bushes in the park.

actividad.pregunta: Mending the puncture costs €8. Dad pays with a €10 note. How much change does he get?

dias.historia: Case solved: the thorn came from a rose bush. The tyre got its puncture by the roses in the park! Now Lucía knows how to mend a puncture, and she does not have to go to the workshop any more.

checklist: I know what a workshop is.
I know that fixing things usually costs less than buying new ones.
I know the steps to mend a puncture.
actividad.prompt: Draw the bike workshop, with its tools.

dias.historia: The club interviews Paco for the school newspaper. Paco says that he opens the school every morning and fixes whatever gets broken, and that he earns a wage for his work.

actividad.pregunta: What does each one do at work?

dias.historia: Paco has been at the school for thirty years. He likes his job, he says, because every day is different: one day he fixes a blind, and another day he makes a snowman.

frases: A wage is the money you earn by working.
Nobody gets paid for any job.
A wage pays for the home and the food.
Paco gets paid for his work at the school.
Only people who wear a tie work.

dias.historia: Paco tells the club a riddle: “I have a face and two hands, but I cannot clap.” It is the school clock, which Paco sets to the right time every Monday!

actividad.pregunta: Is it a job?

dias.historia: Paco shows the club his old trick: writing down in a notebook what comes in and what goes out. Lucía tries it with her money for the week.

actividad.pregunta: Lucía's accounts: how much does she have left after each line?

dias.historia: At the end, Paco remembers something about the capsule: it was buried “at midday, in the shade of the big plane tree, ten steps from the fountain”. But today there are two plane trees, and the fountain is somewhere else...

checklist: I know what a wage is.
I know what Paco does in his job.
I can keep accounts of my money.
actividad.prompt: Draw the job you would like to have when you grow up.

dias.historia: For World Book Day, the class has a book exchange: everyone brings a book they have already read and takes home another one. That way everyone gets a new book without spending any money.
At the end of the exchange, there is one book left over with no name in it, with sand between the pages and sentences underlined in green. Whose can it be?

actividad.pregunta: Is it an exchange?
cosas: You swap one book for another.
You swap cards at break time.
You swap your sandwich for Hugo's.
You pay for a cinema ticket.

dias.historia: Nora and Leo went to the seaside for the Easter holidays, and they both came back with sand in their trainers. Which of them owns the book?

frases: In an exchange, everyone gives something and gets something.
In an exchange, you pay with money.
A book you have already read can be new for someone else.
If you swap a book, you lose it for ever.

dias.historia: At the book fair in the square, Hugo cannot decide between a book about planets and a card album. He only has enough money for one of them.

actividad.pregunta: Hugo has €15: he can afford the book or the card album, but not both. Which would you choose?

dias.historia: Case solved: Leo and Irene both underline in green, but only Leo went to the seaside. The book is Leo's! He gets it back, and swaps it for another one.

checklist: I know what an exchange is.
I know that in an exchange everyone gives and gets.
I can make fair swaps.
actividad.prompt: Draw the book you would take to an exchange.

dias.historia: Paco finds an old plan of the school and the streets around it, with their shops. Some are still the same, like the baker's; others have changed: the shoe shop is now a greengrocer's.

actividad.pregunta: What is sold in each shop?

dias.historia: The club compares the old plan with the neighbourhood today. Where there was a stationer's, there still is one; but a bargain shop has opened next door, and the prices are not the same.

actividad.pregunta: A pencil costs €2 at the stationer's and €1 at the bargain shop. Where is it cheaper? How much do you save?

dias.historia: In the neighbourhood there are shops for everything: bikes, books, toys... Lucía wants to know what she could buy with the €20 she has saved.
According to the old plan, the only tree in the playground was next to the wall on the left. But today there are two plane trees: which of them is the old one?

actividad.pregunta: What is sold at the baker's?

dias.historia: Case solved: the plane tree on the left is the old one, because it is the only one on the plan and it has the thicker trunk. The capsule is getting closer and closer!

checklist: I know what a shop is.
I know what is sold in each shop in my neighbourhood.
I can compare prices between shops.
actividad.prompt: Draw your street, with its shops.

dias.historia: Hugo has a tortoise called Rayo. Having a pet is a responsibility: you have to feed it, clean its home and take it to the vet. And all that costs money.

actividad.pregunta: This week, Hugo buys lettuce, strawberries and a new bucket for Rayo. How much does he spend?

dias.historia: Rayo has disappeared from Hugo's garden. There are half-moon-shaped bites in the lettuces in the vegetable patch. Could it have been him?

frases: A pet needs food every day.
Looking after an animal costs nothing.
Being responsible means doing your part.
Tortoises only eat sweets.

dias.historia: Hugo wants to take Rayo to the vet for a check-up, which costs €30. He already has €12, and every week he will save €6 from his pocket money.

actividad.pregunta: Hugo has €12 and he saves €6 every week. The check-up costs €30. How many weeks will it take?

dias.historia: It was the hottest afternoon of the year, and the soil in Dad's vegetable patch has just been watered. Rayo's tracks suddenly stop...

actividad.pregunta: What does Hugo do to find Rayo?
pasos: He sees that Rayo is missing.
He looks for clues in the garden.

dias.historia: Case solved: because of the heat, Rayo buried himself in the cool soil of the vegetable patch. Hugo promises to check the fence every week: it is his responsibility.

checklist: I know what responsibility is.
I know what a pet needs.
I know that looking after an animal costs money and time.
actividad.prompt: Draw a pet you would like to look after, and what it would need.

dias.historia: For Mother's Day, Lucía and Dani want to give Mum something. They do not have much money, but they do have time: they will make her breakfast and write her a poem.

actividad.pregunta: Does it cost money or time?
cosas: a bunch of flowers from the florist's

dias.historia: On Sunday, Lucía and Dani get up before everyone else. Dad helps them with the juice, and Dani chooses the prettiest flower in the garden for the tray.

actividad.pregunta: How do they make the surprise breakfast?
pasos: They make the juice and the toast.
They put a flower on the tray.

dias.historia: Lucía writes a poem for Mum, and then puts it into the club's code, so that Mum has to crack it. It takes her quite a while, but it is worth it.

actividad.texto: Lucía takes 20 minutes to write the poem and 10 minutes to put it into code. How many minutes does she take altogether?

dias.historia: Mum cracks the poem all by herself: she knows the club's code! “It is the best present,” she says. “You have given me your time.”

frases: Time can be a present too.
A present is only worth something if it is expensive.
Doing something for someone shows them that you love them.
The time we spend together is worth nothing.

dias.historia: In the afternoon, the whole family goes for a walk in the park together. Mum says she has not spent anything all day, and that it has been one of her happiest days.

checklist: I know what time is.
I know that time is a present too.
I can give a present without spending money.
actividad.prompt: Draw a present of time for someone in your family.

dias.historia: For his birthday, Dani gets his first piggy bank, a little pig like Lucía's. Grandma gives him €20 to start it off, and Lucía explains her three jars to him.

actividad.pregunta: Dani has €20. He puts €10 in the save jar and €5 in the share jar. How much does he put in the spend jar?

dias.historia: Dani has been given money by the whole family for his birthday. He puts it all on the table to count it, the way Lucía taught him: first the notes.

actividad.pregunta: How much money has Dani been given?

dias.historia: Now Lucía is Reader X: she sets up a treasure hunt with riddles for Dani. Meanwhile, Dani already knows what he wants to save for: a football.

actividad.pregunta: Dani has €10 and he saves €5 every week. The football costs €25. How many weeks will it take?

dias.historia: The treasure hunt ends at the washing machine: inside there is a red detective notebook, like the green one Lucía found in September. Now Dani is a detective too!

actividad.pregunta: Dani has €5 to spend: he can afford a small ball or a storybook, but not both. Which would you choose?

dias.historia: That night, Dani puts his first coin in his piggy bank. He hears the “clink” and smiles: his football is a little bit closer.

checklist: I know what a piggy bank is.
I know what saving is for.
I can count birthday money.
actividad.prompt: Draw Dani's first piggy bank, and what he wants to buy.

dias.historia: Marta explains that honey goes along a chain before it reaches our homes: the bees, the hive, the beekeeper, the jar and the shop. So much work in one spoonful!

actividad.pregunta: What is the right order? From the flower to the jar of honey
pasos: The bees take nectar from the flowers.
In the hive, they turn it into honey.
The honey is put into jars.
We buy it at the shop.

dias.historia: For days now, bees have been flying to the windows of Lucía's class. Is there a honeycomb? The club investigates carefully, without disturbing them.

actividad.pregunta: Who does each thing in the honey chain?

dias.historia: Grandma buys her honey at the market, from the beekeeper who makes it. She says it is cheaper that way, because there are fewer steps in the chain.

actividad.pregunta: A jar of honey costs €5 at the market and €7 at the supermarket. Where is it cheaper? How much do you save?

dias.historia: All four classroom windows have blue frames, and there is no honeycomb. But on one of them there are pots of lavender, of a beautiful purple...

frases: Honey is made by bees.
Honey grows inside the jars.
Each step in the chain is a job.
Without bees there would be more honey.

dias.historia: Case solved: the bees go to the pots of lavender, because they can see the colour purple very well. Marta decides to leave them: they are part of the honey chain too!

checklist: I know what a chain is.
I know where honey comes from.
I know that each step in the chain is a job.
actividad.prompt: Draw the honey chain, from the flower to the jar.

dias.historia: The class goes to a school farm. There they see where the things we consume every day come from: eggs, milk, cheese, bread...

actividad.pregunta: Where does it come from?

dias.historia: In the morning, the gate of the goat pen is open, and the goats are running all over the farm. Who opened it? Nobody left the hostel all night.

actividad.pregunta: Does it come from the farm?

dias.historia: Each group picks strawberries in the farm's vegetable garden. Lucía's group, four children, picks 17, and they share them out to take home.

actividad.pregunta: Share 17 strawberries between the 4 children in the group. How many does each one get? Are there any left over?

dias.historia: On the latch of the pen there is slobber and tooth marks, and in the mud there are prints of split hooves. And there was no wind at all last night...

actividad.texto: At breakfast, the class drinks 24 glasses of milk, and at teatime, 18. How many glasses does it consume altogether?

dias.historia: Case solved: Lola the goat opened the gate! Some goats learn to open latches. The farmer puts on a new one, and Lola watches very closely.

checklist: I know what consume means.
I know where the food I eat comes from.
I know that we must not waste food.
actividad.prompt: Draw the school farm, with its animals.

dias.historia: The club puts all its clues together to find the capsule. Paco says that the capsule keeps memories, just as the bank keeps money: so that they are safe.

frases: Money is kept at the bank.
The bank lends money too.
The money in the bank belongs to nobody.
Money is safer in the bank than under the bed.
A river bank keeps money.

dias.historia: Grandma opens a savings account for Lucía at the bank. The savings book shows everything: what goes in, what comes out and what is left.

actividad.pregunta: Lucía's savings book: how much is left after each line?

dias.historia: With the clues, the club is sure: ten of Paco's steps from the sandpit, towards the old plane tree... The capsule is in square B3 on the plan!

actividad.prompt: Draw what you think is inside the capsule.

dias.historia: On Thursday, with Marta's permission and Paco's spade, the club digs in B3. Clonk! A rusty red box appears, with a message written backwards on the lid.

actividad.pregunta: What is each thing for?

dias.historia: The message on the lid, read in a mirror, says: “Open at the end-of-year party.” They will have to wait... Only one week!

checklist: I know what a bank is.
I know that money is safe in the bank.
I can write down what goes in and what comes out.
actividad.prompt: Draw the moment when the club finds the capsule.

dias.historia: At the end-of-year party, each class sets up a stall at the market. Lucía's class sells biscuits, second-hand books and pots of flowers. The money they make will go to the library.

actividad.pregunta: A mum buys a bag of biscuits and a book. How much does she pay?

dias.historia: Sofía keeps the stall's accounts: she starts with €10 in coins, so that she can give change, and she writes down every sale in her notebook.

actividad.pregunta: The stall's accounts: how much is there after each line?

dias.historia: Hugo serves the customers. A man buys a flowerpot and pays with a big note: Hugo counts the change twice, so as not to make a mistake.

actividad.pregunta: A flowerpot costs €5. A man pays with a €20 note. How much change does Hugo give him?

dias.historia: At last they open the capsule: inside there are letters from the children of twenty-five years ago. Pilar wanted to be a doctor; Jorge, a firefighter; Ana, a baker... and a letter with no name says: “I want to be a teacher at this school.”

actividad.pregunta: What did each one want to be?

dias.historia: Case solved: the letter with no name is Marta's, the girl holding the box in the photo. And she did it! The club writes its own letter for a new capsule.

checklist: I know what selling is.
I can keep the accounts of a stall.
I can give change without making mistakes.
actividad.prompt: Draw a market stall, and what you would sell.
